records.title: You smell propane inside the RV
questions: I smell propane

What do I do if I smell gas?

records.immediateAction: Put out every flame, ventilate, shut off the propane at the tank, and get everyone outside.
steps: Put out any open flame or pilot light.
Check that all stove and oven knobs are fully turned off.
Turn off the house battery / battery disconnect switch.
Open the windows, roof vents and entry door to let in fresh air.
Step outside and close the propane shut-off valve on the tank.
All occupants leave the area until the smell has gone.
Only after the RV is fully ventilated, the smell has cleared and you have confirmed the source is off may you carefully reset the system.

records.title: Alarm triggered by sprays, perfume or dust
questions: Why did the alarm go off for no reason?
The gas alarm goes off when I use hairspray
Can dust set off the alarm?
symptoms: alarm sounds briefly after using a spray
records.immediateAction: Treat every alarm as real first. Ventilate, then consider a nuisance trigger.
steps: Follow the alarm procedure first: ventilate and check the stove and oven knobs are off.
Once you are satisfied there is no gas smell, ventilate the area and stop using the product near the alarm.
Known nuisance triggers include cleaning sprays, disinfectants, nail polish, perfumes, alcohol, colognes and excess dust.
Generator exhaust and campfire smoke can also trigger the detectors; keep the windows closed when the generator is running or you are parked near a fire.
burningManOverride: Playa dust in the sensor is a recognised nuisance trigger. Excessive dust can set off the carbon-monoxide / LPG alarm.
doNot: Do not disable or disconnect the detector because it is inconvenient.
Do not assume an alarm is a nuisance trigger before you have ventilated and checked for a gas smell.

records.title: Generator will not start
questions: Why won't the generator start?
The generator cranks but will not start
How do I start the generator?
Generator won't turn over
symptoms: generator cranks but does not fire
generator does not crank at all
records.immediateAction: Turn off the A/C, microwave and plugged-in appliances, then check fuel and coach battery.
steps: Confirm the roof air conditioning, microwave and anything plugged into the outlets are switched off.
Check the fuel gauge. The generator shares the engine fuel tank and will not run below a quarter tank.
If the generator will not crank, the coach battery is likely low. Start the RV engine, then start the generator.
If the generator has not run in 24 hours, press and hold the STOP/PRIME end of the switch until the indicator light comes on, then press and hold START.
If it does not start within 15 seconds, release the switch, wait 30 seconds and hold START again.
If it still will not start from the inside switch, try the START/STOP switch on the generator itself.
burningManOverride: Do not run the generator or engine during a dust storm. Dust can clog the air filter and damage the engine or generator.
The generator uses the engine's gasoline and shuts off automatically at a quarter tank. Expect roughly 25 to 40 hours of generator use at about one gallon per hour.

records.title: Charging the coach batteries at Burning Man
questions: How do I keep the batteries charged?
How often should I run the engine?
Dry camping power schedule
How long do I run the generator to charge?
records.immediateAction: At Burning Man: run the engine one hour, at least three times a day — or run the generator for eight hours.
steps: Keep the coach battery switch ON at all times, or the batteries do not get charged.
Charge on the Burning Man schedule below rather than the ordinary dry-camping schedule.
While the generator is running, use the power-hungry appliances and charge phones and laptops.
Check the coach battery status by pressing and holding the BATT button on the monitor panel with the generator and engine off and shore power disconnected.
If the display is not reading at least Fair, charge it. A full charge can take four hours or more.
burningManOverride: Unless you are connected to external power, start the engine at least 3 times per day and run for one hour each time, especially before going to sleep.
Alternatively, run the generator for 8 hours.
The coach battery switch MUST always be ON or the batteries do not get charged.
For a 12-volt refrigerator it is critical to maintain the house battery charge more often.

The outlets are not working

Press the RESET button on the GFCI outlet — usually in the bathroom, but it may be in the galley or on an exterior outlet.
If the breakers keep tripping, turn off appliances and unplug personal items, then reset again.
